before.title: [GO, UP, MX] Live Preview of Content in CMS

after.description: As a Content Author, I want to preview draft entries in CMS so that I can see how content will be shown on the website. This requires initializing the Contentstack Live Preview SDK on the client side, registering the onEntryChange callback within the ContentstackContext provider, and re-fetching/updating context data when the callback fires so the entire component tree re-renders with draft content. Preview URL configuration is done in the Contentstack web app UI, not in application code. Limitation: protected pages and content may not be previewable.
after.title: [GO, UP, MX] Live Preview of Content in CMS
verificationCriteria: Given the application is loaded in a non-preview environment (no live-preview SDK initialization), all existing content renders identically to the current production behavior — no visual or functional regression.

The Contentstack Live Preview SDK initialization call includes the required configuration parameters (stack API key, delivery token, environment, and any other parameters mandated by the SDK) sourced from the application's existing environment configuration.
The application does not contain hardcoded preview URL patterns; preview URL routing is handled entirely by the Contentstack web app configuration (Stack Settings > Live Preview).

notes: This is a novel capability — the codebase currently has a static ContentstackContext with no live-preview subscription. The Contentstack Live Preview SDK must be initialized client-side and wired into the context provider so that onEntryChange triggers a re-render with draft data. Documentation confirms: (1) onEntryChange takes NO argument — it signals that a change occurred and the app must re-fetch; (2) preview URL configuration lives in the Contentstack web app UI, not in application code; (3) the SDK targets Next.js CSR with App Router. The attachment point is ContentstackContext.Provider, consumed by 40+ components via useContent. The hook file src/hooks/useContent.ts is the consumer-side integration point. Unreachable external services: contentstack.io, contentstack.com, api.contentstack.io, cdn.contentstack.io — criteria stop at our side of that boundary.

notes: Openspec provided empty acceptanceCriteria with rich contextual notes about the current architecture. All 14 criteria above are new. Key design decisions: (1) AC-1/AC-3 cover the core re-render behavior — observable via component output, not implementation; (2) AC-2/AC-6/AC-7 ensure zero-impact when preview is not active — critical for production safety; (3) AC-4 addresses SSR safety since this is a Next.js App Router project and the current context has no browser dependency; (4) AC-5 covers error resilience for the re-fetch triggered by onEntryChange; (5) AC-8 addresses the real-world edge case of rapid successive signals causing render thrashing; (6) AC-9 enforces the stated limitation about protected content not being previewable and prevents auth bypass; (7) AC-10 adds an accessibility/UX requirement — content authors must be able to distinguish preview from live; (8) AC-11 ensures type safety is maintained for the 40+ consuming components; (9) AC-12/AC-13 cover the full preview lifecycle including entry switching and session teardown; (10) AC-14 ensures no SSR bundle bloat. I could not verify the package.json contents for existing Contentstack SDK dependencies due to tool call limits, but the search for 'contentstack' in package.json returned no matches, suggesting no live-preview SDK is installed yet. I also could not locate the Provider component wrapping site — it likely exists in a layout or app file not found by search. If the provider has additional complexity, AC-3 and AC-11 may need further refinement.
